subject: Re: Long-context evals: context window fit & truncation behavior (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Long-context evals: context window fit & truncation behavior — post-call recap

Alex / Eval team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — productive session. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment on scope and what we'll deliver in the trial evaluation: 

Summary of needs (from call):
- Evaluate how models handle >64k token conversation histories (truncation behavior, fidelity of summarization).
- Measure quality regressions when we apply quantization/4-bit variants on long-context inputs.
- Validate prefix/KV cache effectiveness for repeated user sessions (latency and token cost).

What Redwood will provide for the trial:
- A baseline evaluation run using 3 recommended model variants (open and quantized): Mistral-40B-Long (full FP16), Mistral-40B-Long-4q (4-bit quantized), and Redwood-Ref-13B-Long (efficient long-context variant).
- Benchmark artifact (summary + per-test-case metrics) and raw CSV/XLSX of token-level outputs.
- The prompt set we discussed (attached: prompt_set_v2.jsonl) with ~120 long-context test cases (mix of nested threads, appended documents, and system instructions).
- Notes on failure modes we observed (truncation points, hallucination patterns, and summarization drift).

Key asks from Acme to proceed:
1) Confirm which data masks we should apply to redacted PII in the test set (we used <REDACTED_EMAIL> by default).
2) Share any specific SLA/latency thresholds for online inference vs batch evaluation (affects our runtime config).
3) Give us a single contact for procurement/PO if you want Redwood to provision Dedicated capacity for sustained runs.

Attachments: acme_long_context_eval_results.xlsx (initial baseline), prompt_set_v2.jsonl (test cases).

Proposed timeline:
- Baseline run by Mon 2026-06-15
- Deep dive call with results and action items Wed 2026-06-17
If that works, I’ll start the baseline run tomorrow.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Marissa,

Appreciate the clear recap — this is exactly the kind of structure we wanted. A couple quick clarifications: 

- For PII redaction, please keep <REDACTED_EMAIL> and <REDACTED_NAME> placeholders; we cannot share raw emails.
- Latency thresholds: for online inference our product team wants 95th percentile < 600ms for user-facing summarization flows; for batch analyses you can ignore that constraint.
- Procurement: Rachel Kim (rachel.kim@acme.com) will own the PO; she’s looped on procurement emails separately.

Two asks on the eval design: 
1) Can you include an evaluation that measures summary fidelity as we increase context length in increments (8k / 16k / 32k / 64k) so we can see degradation curves?
2) Any chance you can surface token-cost-per-accepted-summary (i.e., cost to produce the portion of the summary that meets our fidelity threshold)?

If you can add those items to the baseline run, we’ll be in a great spot for Wed.

Thanks,
Alex
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Corporation

Subject: Re: Long-context evals: context window fit & truncation behavior — baseline plan and recommended models

Alex — quick technical follow-up from the infra side. Adding the fidelity sweep (8k/16k/32k/64k) is straightforward; we’ll run the same 120 test cases at each length and compute ROUGE/CL-E/F1 plus a summary-similarity metric you suggested. A few notes and recommendations: 

Recommended model variants for the trial (tradeoffs):
- mistral-40b-long (fp16) — best quality baseline for long-context; higher cost but minimal regression on summaries.
- mistral-40b-long-4q (4-bit) — ~2-2.5x cost reduction on token generation; expect modest degradation on fine-grained factual recall inside summaries (we’ll flag per-case regressions).
- redwood-ref-13b-long (optimized) — good latency profile, lower token cost; may struggle on deeply nested instruction-following cases.

Benchmark links (internal):
- Long-context benchmark dashboard: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFGacme-long-context-evals
- Raw outputs (CSV/XLSX) attached in baseline artifact: acme_long_context_eval_results.xlsx

Prompt & eval notes: 
- prompt_set_v2.jsonl includes control tokens that enforce extractive vs abstractive summarization. We’ll include a separate column marking which test cases require extractive fidelity vs synthesis.
- Truncation behavior: we’ll instrument token-origin mapping so you can see which source spans contributed to each summary sentence. This helps detect silent truncation (missing critical context due to early cut).
- Cache strategy: for repeated-session runs we’ll use session-aware prefix caching; I’ll include token-cost deltas with and without caching enabled.

Expected deliverables for the baseline run (Mon):
- Per-model CSV with per-case metrics (ROUGE-L, BLEU, CL score), per-case token counts, and flags for regression cases.
- Aggregate degradation curves (8k->64k) and a short executive summary (one page).

Let me know if you want us to add any additional eval metrics (e.g., factuality via Q&A probes).

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
